images.title: Odd numbers wrap into a square
images.purpose: Shows a 6 by 6 square of dots built from inverted L shapes of 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 and 11 dots, so the first 6 odd numbers add to 36.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One large square grid of dots in the centre, with small numbers above its columns and one result label below.
images.exact_structure: A 6 by 6 square of equal round dots, 36 dots in all, rows numbered 1 to 6 from the top and columns 1 to 6 from the left (numbers not shown). Layer k is every dot whose row or column, whichever is larger, equals k: layer 1 is the top left dot (1 dot), layer 2 is 3 dots, layer 3 is 5 dots, layer 4 is 7 dots, layer 5 is 9 dots, layer 6 is 11 dots, each an inverted L shape. Layers 1, 3 and 5 are filled teal (#0072B2); layers 2, 4 and 6 are filled amber (#E69F00). Above the grid, over column k, sits the dot count of layer k: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11. Below the grid, centred: 6 × 6 = 36. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: The first n odd numbers add up to n².
images.description: Shows a 6 by 6 square of dots built from inverted L shapes of 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 and 11 dots, so the first 6 odd numbers add to 36.

image_decisions.why: The inverted L picture is the visual proof that sums of the first odd numbers are squares.
